text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — ACME is asking for Private/VPC hardware guidance for a July->Aug customer ramp. They quoted ~6,000,000 tokens/day peak. Model mix: llama-2-13b-q4 + gpt-compat-7b. Need a quick sizing estimate (GPU count, GPU-hours), rack/power notes for eu-west, and a fallback plan if regional capacity is tight.

Ajay Patel: Quick back-of-envelope calc so we have something for sales. assumptions below. happy to refine after Rachel checks inventory. :mag:
```
assumptions:
- peak_tokens_day = 6_000_000
- avg_tokens_per_request = 150
- tokens_per_gpu_sec (13b-q4 @ A100-80GB) ~ 60 tok/s (sustained batch)
compute:
requests_per_day = peak_tokens_day / avg_tokens_per_request = 40_000 req/day
tokens_per_gpu_day = tokens_per_gpu_sec * 86400 = 5_184_000 tok/day
required_gpus = ceil(peak_tokens_day / tokens_per_gpu_day) = ceil(6_000_000 / 5_184_000) = 2 GPUs
notes: this is pure throughput. Add concurrency/latency headroom => recommend 3-4 GPUs + autoscale for bursts.
```

Rachel Gomez: eu-west note — we often can't get A100-80 in immediate availability. Typical options: A100-40, A40, or multi-A10 pools. Two points: rack PDUs at customer sites sometimes limit to 10-12kW/customer (so 2x A100 racks may exceed), and NVLink topologies differ (in-cloud vs on-prem). If customer expects <200ms p95, we should target extra concurrency and smaller batch sizes.

Michael O'Neill: +1 on headroom. Suggest baseline proposal: 4x A100-80GB as primary (if available) with 2x A40 fallback nodes in the same VPC for overflow. Also recommend a small burst pool in adjacent region (eu-central) with automated routing if eu-west capacity drops below 70%. Pre-warm KV cache before peak windows to shave cold-starts.

Ajay Patel: Updated calc for evening peak (3x baseline traffic for a short window). If peak multiplier = 3, required_gpus ~ 6 (with same perf assumptions). So recommend autoscale policy: baseline 4, scale-to 8 for 20-minute windows, cooldown 15m.

CapacityPlanner-bot: Ticket CP-3847 created: "ACME Private sizing + eu-west fallback" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CP-3847 

Maria Chen: Action items:
- @Ajay Patel: build a detailed GPU-hours spreadsheet (baseline/peak/3-month forecast).
- @Rachel Gomez: validate eu-west hardware inventory and vendor lead times; flag if A100-80 not available.
- @Michael O'Neill: draft routing/fallback policy and burst pool config (eu-central).
I'll send a short note to sales with the 4x baseline / 8x burst numbers and the ticket.

Rachel Gomez: FYI — also check customer rack power at their colo provider. If they do on-prem, we may need to split nodes across two racks to remain under PDUs.

Ajay Patel: I’ll drop the spreadsheet in CP-3847 by EOD tomorrow.

Maria Chen: Thanks team :pray: — keeping this thread for updates.
